primary_cartographic_boundary_record.title: Burundi – Democratic Republic of the Congo (Zaire) Boundary, International Boundary Study No. 48
primary_cartographic_boundary_record.publisher_authorship: The Geographer, Office of the Geographer, Bureau of Intelligence and Research, U.S. Department of State
findings: The report describes the northern land segment as following the thalweg of the Rusizi/Ruzizi and its Rusizi Rutoya (Petite Ruzizi) branch, from Lake Tanganyika toward the Rwanda tripoint.
It attributes the present Burundi–Congo boundary to the Belgium–Germany convention of 1910, ratifications exchanged in 1911, and cites a 1911 demarcation protocol approved by 1912 notes.
It states that no official boundary area was then known to be disputed, while noting recent unofficial Congolese claims concerning the delta between the Rusizi Rutoya and Rusizi.
cartographic_references_named_by_report: Rwanda and Burundi Series 1301, Edition 2, published 1964 at 1:500,000
primary_cartographic_boundary_record.limits: This is a State Department boundary study that quotes or cites historical instruments; it is not itself the signed 1910 convention, and its named maps are historical regional sheets. It gives no surveyed coordinates for these three modern raster-cell centers and does not establish which side of the thalweg any center lies on. Its historical statement about unofficial delta claims is not a finding that these three points fall within that claimed delta.

interpretation: The primary study supplies relevant historical legal/cartographic context for the South Kivu contact corridor and identifies a thalweg-based boundary plus a localized delta claim. The exact three retained cells are land-class centers with COD ADM1 contact; the report alone cannot resolve their exact source membership or current ownership. Their contact remains an adverse competitor requiring a finer, lawful exact-location witness, without inferring that every COD contact is a sovereignty dispute.
excluded_work: No Stanford, Assembly, CENI, or SALB-term access retry
